summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted following a fall from bed, with concerns for injury and a supratherapeutic INR of 11.9. Imaging showed no acute fractures or intracranial abnormalities. The elevated INR, likely due to warfarin interaction with recent antibiotics, was reversed with vitamin K, and anticoagulation was carefully resumed. Initially asymptomatic bacteriuria with Morganella was treated when urinary symptoms developed. She developed right thigh cellulitis during admission, confirmed on ultrasound without DVT, and was treated with doxycycline. A midline catheter was placed for IV ertapenem to complete outpatient antibiotic therapy. Her chronic conditions, including HIV, hepatitis B/C, diastolic heart failure, and asthma, were managed throughout. She was discharged home with home health support, a bariatric bed, wheelchair, and a plan for close follow-up.
